other.mold: cylindrical steel molds of 42 mm diameter

evidence.quote: The alloy Mg 98.5Y1Zn0.5 (at %) was obtained by melting high purity Mg and Zn as well as a Mg-22%Y (wt %) master alloy in an electric resistance furnace. The mixture was then cast in cylindrical steel molds of 42 mm in diameter.
Chip and powder compacts and cast cylinders machined up 40 mm were extruded at 350 ◦C using several extrusion ratios depending on the material: 4:1 and 18:1 for the cast alloy
the machined chips were fabricated by high-speed machining in a conventional Computer numerical controlled (CNC) lathe
Chips and powders were uniaxial compacted under 350 MPa for 2 min at room temperature (RT), providing cylindrical green compacts of 40 mm in diameter.

Chip and powder compacts and cast cylinders machined up 40 mm were extruded at 350 ◦C using several extrusion ratios depending on the material: 4:1 and 18:1 for the cast alloy and 36:1 for the chip and powder compacts.

RS powders were prepared by the EIGA (Electrode Induction Melting Gas Atomization) process by TLS Technik GmbH (Bitterfeld-Wolfen, Germany). Powders have a spherical morphology with a diameter less than 100 µm.
Chips and powders were uniaxial compacted under 350 MPa for 2 min at room temperature (RT), providing cylindrical green compacts of 40 mm in diameter.

Chip and powder compacts and cast cylinders machined up 40 mm were extruded at 350 ◦C using several extrusion ratios depending on the material: 4:1 and 18:1 for the cast alloy and 36:1 for the chip and powder compacts.

parameters.time: 5 min heating to die temperature per pass
parameters.deformation: true strain 0.7 per pass, up to four passes

evidence.quote: Cylinders from the extruded cast alloy bar, 70 mm long and 20 mm in diameter (extrusion ratio 4:1) were ECAP processed at 300 ◦C, using route B (i.e., 90◦ rotation of the sample between passes).
Results are compared to those obtained in Mg 97Y2Zn1 alloy processed by the extrusion of the as-cast material.
The interdendritic phase was characterized by a lamellar morphology typical of the LPSO-phase. The volume fraction of the LPSO-phase was 9%
a two-phase dendritic microstructure consisting of magnesium dendrites with a second phase located at the interdendritic space
The micrograph of the Mg 98.5Y1Zn0.5 cast alloy (Figure 2a) revealed a two-phase dendritic microstructure

the LPSO-phase appeared to be homogeneously and finely distributed in the magnesium matrix with a particle size below 500 nm (Figure 3d). These LPSO-phase particles were located mainly at grain boundaries
the LPSO-phase was fragmented into small particles with a diameter lower than 1 µm
After extrusion, the LPSO-phase in the CE material appeared strongly elongated along the extrusion direction

attributes.morphology: elongated along initial extrusion direction with serrated shape distribution

evidence.quote: The LPSO-phase in the CEE material was still elongated along the initial extrusion direction but also showed a serrated shape distribution after each pass by ECAP

attributes.morphology: fine DRXed grains and coarse non-recrystallized grains elongated along extrusion direction

evidence.quote: The CE material showed a bimodal grain structure with DRXed grains of about 1 µm and non-DRXed coarse grains elongated along the extrusion direction.
The CME material was fully recrystallized with a grain size slightly lower than that of the extruded as-cast ingots (1.08 µm).
Finally, the PME material was fully recrystallized with a grain size of 0.96 µm.

attributes.morphology: intimately mixed recrystallized and non-recrystallized grains

evidence.quote: The alloy processed using ECAP was not completely recrystallized.
much lower than volume fraction in the Mg 97Y2Zn1 alloy, which was between 20% and 25%
The optimization of extrusion parameters of as-cast Mg97Y2Zn1 ingots results in a material combining cast high-yield stress (around 350 MPa) and appreciable ductility
The extrusion of RS ribbons with a very fine dendritic microstructure renders a yield stress of 410 MPa
A yield stress similar to that found for extruded Mg 97Y2Zn1 alloy can be attained with only half of the usual yttrium and zinc additions thanks to the grain refinement induced by ECAP processing.

The presence of the LPSO-phase as small particles rendered a more homogeneous distribution of this phase within the magnesium matrix, acting as pinning points which prevented further coarsening of the DRXed grains.
the decrease in the Y concentration implies a significant decrease in mechanical strength because the volume fraction of the reinforcing LPSO-phase is reduced
